metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent pressed M to activate the Move tool, then dragged the text layer slightly to the left, but never exported or saved the PNG. Original evaluator found no PNG, resulting in reward=0.
metadata.capability_extraction: Agent can activate GIMP tools via keyboard shortcut (M for Move), select the active layer, and drag layers around the canvas.
metadata.failure_analysis: Agent stopped after moving the text without exporting to PNG. The task instruction now explicitly requires the PNG export so the evaluator can verify the text position.
metadata.task_rationale: Direct simplification of the failed task: require the agent to perform the same left-shift of the text AND export as PNG so the evaluator has a file to read. Anchored to the reliable prefix action 'key; text=m'.
metadata.explanation: The getter downloads /home/user/Desktop/orange_background.png from the VM, locates dark (text) pixels, and returns their horizontal center. The metric returns 1.0 if the text center x is in the left half of the image. Initial state has no PNG on the Desktop, so the initial score is 0.0 (negative-control safe).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads the exported PNG from the expected Desktop path, implicitly verifying the export requirement.
Dark pixel heuristic (all RGB channels < 80) correctly identifies black text against an orange background, as orange pixels have G ~165 and would not trigger this threshold.
Metric correctly checks if text horizontal center is in the left half (text_center_x < width // 2), which is a reasonable interpretation of 'left side of the canvas'.
Negative-control resistant: no PNG exists on the Desktop in the initial state, so the getter returns an error dict and the metric returns 0.0.
Both task requirements are covered: (1) PNG exported to Desktop and (2) text positioned on the left half of the canvas.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: 'left side' is slightly ambiguous - using width//3 or width//4 as the threshold would more strictly enforce 'left side' rather than just 'left half', but left half is an acceptable interpretation.

Minor: if the image contains other dark elements besides the text (e.g., icons or other artifacts), the dark pixel centroid could be misleading; using a minimum dark pixel count threshold or bounding box approach would improve specificity.
